title: Monotone diagrams under degree prefixes and essential restriction
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbf N$ and let $D\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ be closed under addition by $\mathbf N^n$ and under each operation $\alpha\mapsto\alpha-\alpha_p e_p+\alpha_p e_v$ for $p<v$. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s$ enumerate its coordinatewise minimal elements in increasing lexicographic order of $(|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$. Set $d_i=|\alpha_i|$ and $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{h<i}(\alpha_h+\mathbf N^n)\}$, as in supported homogeneous division [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. For $u\in\mathbf N$, put $I_u=\{i:d_i\le u\}$ and $D_{\le u}=\bigcup_{i\in I_u}(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$. Then $D_{\le u}$ is additive and closed under the same coordinate moves; its ordered minimal vertices are exactly the retained $\alpha_i$, and their quotient supports are the original $\Delta_i$. Put $J=\{j:\exists i,\alpha_i(j)>0\}$ with its inherited order. This is a final segment of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For $\bar\alpha_i=\alpha_i|_J$ the diagram $\bar D=\bigcup_i(\bar\alpha_i+\mathbf N^J)$ is additive and closed under the whole-coordinate moves between ordered indices of $J$, and $(\bar\alpha_i)$ is exactly its ordered minimal vertex family, with unchanged degrees. If $\iota:\mathbf N^J\to\mathbf N^n$ extends by zero outside $J$, then
$$\bar\Delta_i=\{\beta\in\mathbf N^J:\iota(\beta)\in\Delta_i\},\qquad\mathbf N^J\setminus\bar D=\{\gamma:\iota(\gamma)\notin D\}.$$
The same restriction assertions hold separately for each $D_{\le u}$, using its own essential-variable set $J_u=\{j:\exists i\in I_u,\alpha_i(j)>0\}$. These conclusions include empty prefixes, $D=\varnothing$, $D=\mathbf N^n$ and $n=0$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the inherited route; Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Section 7, condition (7.2)(2), and section 8 applied in Theorem 9.6, printed p.282: degree prefixes and restriction to variables occurring in vertices; combinatorial preservation assertions written out by the agent. Journal PDF read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf. No Stacks tag states this specialized result; BM paper absent from repository literature.

proof.text: Write $a\le b$ for coordinatewise comparison. For $x\in D$, the finite nonempty set $\{a\in D:a\le x\}$ has an element $a$ of least total degree. If $b\in D$, $b\le a$ and $b\ne a$, then $|b|<|a|$, a contradiction. Hence $a$ is a listed minimal vertex. Conversely, any vector dominating a vertex belongs to $D$ by additive closure. Thus $x\in D$ if and only if $\alpha_h\le x$ for some $h$. This uses only the finite vertex list already assumed in the statement, not a finiteness theorem for all antichains.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument for the combinatorial preservation assertion; compare Bierstone–Milman 1997, §7 (7.1), pp.261–262, and §8, p.273, read online at the journal PDF URL in source.place. ILO VIII 2.3.11–2.3.13, pp.93–94, supplies only the inherited parent route.

proof.text: The set $I_u$ is an initial segment because degrees are nondecreasing in the prescribed ordering. The union defining $D_{\le u}$ is additive. Every retained vertex remains minimal: a smaller element of $D_{\le u}\subseteq D$ would contradict its minimality in $D$. Conversely a minimal element of the union dominates some retained vertex and must equal it. The inherited ordering is therefore the required degree-lexicographic ordering. For retained $i$, every $h<i$ is retained, since $d_h\le d_i\le u$; hence the earlier-vertex union defining its quotient support is identical to the original one in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. This proves the asserted equality of supports without any reindexing ambiguity.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument for the combinatorial preservation assertion; compare Bierstone–Milman 1997, §7 (7.1), pp.261–262, and §8, p.273, read online at the journal PDF URL in source.place. ILO VIII 2.3.11–2.3.13, pp.93–94, supplies only the inherited parent route.

proof.text: Fix $p<v$ and let $T(x)=x-x_p e_p+x_p e_v$. Coordinatewise, $T$ sets coordinate $p$ to zero, replaces coordinate $v$ by $x_v+x_p$, and leaves the others unchanged. In particular $T(x+y)=T(x)+T(y)$ and $|T(x)|=|x|$. If $x=\alpha_i+b\in D_{\le u}$, monotonicity of $D$ gives $T(\alpha_i)\in D$. Step 1 gives a vertex $\alpha_h\le T(\alpha_i)$, whence $d_h\le|T(\alpha_i)|=d_i\le u$. Thus $T(x)=\alpha_h+(T(\alpha_i)-\alpha_h)+T(b)$ lies in $D_{\le u}$. Subtraction here is coordinatewise between comparable nonnegative vectors. This proves closure under every required move, including $x_p=0$.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument for the combinatorial preservation assertion; compare Bierstone–Milman 1997, §7 (7.1), pp.261–262, and §8, p.273, read online at the journal PDF URL in source.place. ILO VIII 2.3.11–2.3.13, pp.93–94, supplies only the inherited parent route.

proof.text: Suppose $p\in J$ and $p<v$. Choose $i$ with $\alpha_i(p)>0$. If $v\notin J$, every vertex has zero $v$th coordinate. By monotonicity and Step 1, there is a vertex $\alpha_h\le T(\alpha_i)$. At $p$ it is zero; at $v$ it is zero by the supposition; elsewhere it is at most $\alpha_i$. Consequently $\alpha_h\le\alpha_i$ and the inequality is strict at $p$, contradicting minimality of $\alpha_i$. Thus $v\in J$. This is precisely that $J$ is a final segment, with the empty segment allowed.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument for the combinatorial preservation assertion; compare Bierstone–Milman 1997, §7 (7.1), pp.261–262, and §8, p.273, read online at the journal PDF URL in source.place. ILO VIII 2.3.11–2.3.13, pp.93–94, supplies only the inherited parent route.

proof.text: Every vertex vanishes off $J$, so $\iota(\bar\alpha_i)=\alpha_i$. For any $\gamma\in\mathbf N^J$ one has $\bar\alpha_i\le\gamma$ if and only if $\alpha_i\le\iota(\gamma)$. The same coordinate check shows that restriction and zero extension preserve and reflect comparisons between vertices, and preserve their degrees. Thus the restricted vertices are distinct and pairwise incomparable. A minimal element of their generated union equals a generating vertex, and a vector of the union below a generating vertex must equal it. This proves that these are exactly its minimal vertices. For unequal vertices the first differing coordinate belongs to $J$, all deleted coordinates being zero in both; hence restriction preserves their degree-lexicographic ordering. Additivity of the generated union is immediate by adding to its witness vertex.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument for the combinatorial preservation assertion; compare Bierstone–Milman 1997, §7 (7.1), pp.261–262, and §8, p.273, read online at the journal PDF URL in source.place. ILO VIII 2.3.11–2.3.13, pp.93–94, supplies only the inherited parent route.

proof.text: By Step 1 and the comparison in Step 5, $\gamma\in\bar D$ if and only if $\iota(\gamma)\in D$, proving the complementary-support equality. If $p<v$ are in $J$ and $\gamma\in\bar D$, zero extension commutes with the coordinate move: $\iota(T\gamma)=T(\iota\gamma)$. The latter belongs to $D$, so $T\gamma\in\bar D$. Finally, by the quotient-support definition in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], $\beta\in\bar\Delta_i$ means that no $h<i$ satisfies $\bar\alpha_h\le\bar\alpha_i+\beta$. Step 5 identifies each such inequality with $\alpha_h\le\alpha_i+\iota\beta$; the absence of these inequalities means exactly $\iota\beta\in\Delta_i$. This proves both support identities and the required closure.

proof.text: Steps 2–3 show that each prefix meets the original hypotheses with exactly its retained ordered vertices. Apply the arguments of Steps 4–6 to that diagram and that list, using its own set $J_u$; this gives all the asserted prefix restriction statements. For an empty list the generated diagram is empty, the essential set is empty, there are no quotient supports, and its complement in $\mathbf N^{\varnothing}=\{0\}$ is $\{0\}$. This covers empty prefixes and $D=\varnothing$. For $D=\mathbf N^n$ the sole vertex is $0$, every $u\in\mathbf N$ retains it, $J=\varnothing$, the restricted diagram is $\{0\}$, its quotient support is $\{0\}$, and both complements are empty. If $n=0$, $\mathbf N^0=\{0\}$, so these empty and full cases exhaust the possibilities; all coordinate moves are vacuous.

lean.statement: theorem monotone_prefix_essential_restriction (n s : ℕ) (D : Set (Fin n →₀ ℕ)) (a : Fin s → Fin n →₀ ℕ) (hD : IsMonotone D) (ha : IsOrderedVertexFamily D a) : (∀ u : ℕ, IsMonotone (generated (prefixVertices a u)) ∧ IsOrderedVertexFamily (generated (prefixVertices a u)) (prefixVertices a u) ∧ ∀ i : {i : Fin s // (a i).degree ≤ u}, quotientSupport (prefixVertices a u) i = quotientSupport a i.val) ∧ ((∀ p v : Fin n, p < v → (∃ i : Fin s, a i p ≠ 0) → ∃ i : Fin s, a i v ≠ 0) ∧ IsMonotone (generated (essentialVertices a)) ∧ IsOrderedVertexFamily (generated (essentialVertices a)) (essentialVertices a) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, (essentialVertices a i).degree = (a i).degree) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, quotientSupport (essentialVertices a) i = {b : EssentialVariables a →₀ ℕ | Finsupp.embDomain (Function.Embedding.subtype _) b ∈ quotientSupport a i}) ∧ (generated (essentialVertices a))ᶜ = {g : EssentialVariables a →₀ ℕ | Finsupp.embDomain (Function.Embedding.subtype _) g ∉ D}) ∧ (∀ u : ℕ, (∀ p v : Fin n, p < v → (∃ i : {i : Fin s // (a i).degree ≤ u}, prefixVertices a u i p ≠ 0) → ∃ i : {i : Fin s // (a i).degree ≤ u}, prefixVertices a u i v ≠ 0) ∧ IsMonotone (generated (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u))) ∧ IsOrderedVertexFamily (generated (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u))) (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u)) ∧ (∀ i : {i : Fin s // (a i).degree ≤ u}, (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u) i).degree = (prefixVertices a u i).degree) ∧ (∀ i : {i : Fin s // (a i).degree ≤ u}, quotientSupport (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u)) i = {b : EssentialVariables (prefixVertices a u) →₀ ℕ | Finsupp.embDomain (Function.Embedding.subtype _) b ∈ quotientSupport (prefixVertices a u) i}) ∧ (generated (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a u)))ᶜ = {g : EssentialVariables (prefixVertices a u) →₀ ℕ | Finsupp.embDomain (Function.Embedding.subtype _) g ∉ generated (prefixVertices a u)})
